topic: Go-bag when you can't carry 10 kg: wheelchair users, people with disabilities and older adults

content.hook: Go-bags are heavy. Yours needn't be.

scenes.text: Pack *light*: documents, money, key medicines first
Add a *support network* who can reach you
A plan that fits *your* body and home

content.caption:
Go-bag for wheelchair users, people with disabilities and older adults: keep it light. A bag you can actually carry works better than a perfect one you can't.

Where to start:
• Keep the bag light. Essentials only: documents, some cash, a list of your medicines, a phone charger.
• Keep bulkier supplies at home, in a spot you can reach easily.
• If you use a wheelchair, think about a small repair and power kit.
• Agree on a support network: neighbours, family or friends who know how to reach you.

Ready72h has a section for this, based on Canadian Red Cross and Christopher & Dana Reeve Foundation guidance.
